title: Licence classes and what this add-on does not grant
moduleTitle: Optional add-on: high-risk work and platform licences
audience: Workers and supervisors who may be asked to work at height or on a platform. Optional add-on, taken alongside the main courses.
learningOutcomes: Identify the states in this add-on that list a boom-type elevating work platform class as a high-risk work licence.
State that this add-on grants no licence, certificate or authority.

instruction.heading: What a high-risk work licence is
instruction.body: Some plant and platform work is licensed as high-risk work. WorkSafe Victoria's high risk work licence page names a boom-type elevating work platform operation licence as a class (page reviewed 30 June 2026). SafeWork NSW also lists a boom-type elevating work platform (WP) class among its high-risk work licences (page last modified 15 June 2026).

instruction.heading: What this add-on does not do
instruction.body: This add-on explains the licence rules. It does not grant a licence, certificate or authority for any regulated work, and finishing it does not qualify a learner to operate a boom-type platform. Check the rule for the state or territory where the work is done with that regulator before any work at height or on a platform.

instruction.heading: How to use this add-on
instruction.body: Take this add-on alongside the main courses. Each lesson marks the points that no official source confirms, so that they are checked before anyone relies on them.

procedure: Name the state or territory where the work will be done.
Open the regulator's high-risk work licence page for that state.
Record the page date and the rule before starting the job.

workedExamples.situation: A tradesperson who has finished this add-on is asked to clean upper walls from a boom-type platform in Victoria.
workedExamples.decisionPrompt: Does finishing the add-on allow the work to start?
workedExamples.reasoning: No. The add-on grants no licence. Victoria's WP class is a high risk work licence class, and whether it applies to this platform depends on the boom length, which is not confirmed by an official source for Victoria (see lesson 3).

commonErrors.error: Treating the add-on as a licence.
commonErrors.prevention: Read the licence notice at the start of every lesson before any licence question.

safetyAndRegulatory.point: Licence notice: this add-on does not grant a licence, certificate or authority for regulated work. Completing it is not a licence for any high-risk work.
Check the licence rule with the state or territory regulator before any work above ground level or with a boom-type platform.

qualityStandard: Learner states that the add-on grants no licence before answering any licence question.
documentationEvidence: Date and URL of the regulator page checked for the state where the work is done.
summary: A WP licence class is named by regulators in Victoria and New South Wales.
This add-on grants no licence or authority.

knowledgeChecks.question: What does completing this add-on give a learner?
options: A high-risk work licence for boom-type platforms
Knowledge only; it does not grant a licence, certificate or authority
A licence number that is valid in every state

officialReferences.title: High risk work licence (WorkSafe Victoria)
officialReferences.covers: Names the boom-type elevating work platform operation licence class; states the class without a boom length; scissor lifts do not need the WP licence. Does not state whether the class applies at any boom length.

officialReferences.title: High-risk work licences (SafeWork NSW)
officialReferences.pageDate: Last modified 15 June 2026 (page metadata; no date shown on page)
officialReferences.covers: Lists the boom-type elevating work platform (WP) class; WP licence where the boom is 11 metres or more.
